correctness.rationale: Exact beta-moment orthogonality yields the specified bilateral weighted shift; inverse powers grow at most polynomially and imply unit-circle spectrum and an operator-norm Laurent resolvent. The cross block factors as an outer product, whose two vector norms are summed by a binomial series. The other two blocks have power exponent (alpha+3)/2 strictly below the cross exponent alpha+2. Exact exterior norm follows from contraction and spectral distance. Normalization and angle invariance are explicit; finite sections are only supplementary.

value.rationale: A nonnormal coordinate operator has the same unit-circle spectrum for every alpha but a highly asymmetric weighted-parameter-dependent pseudospectral thickness. The exact rank-one cross-channel mechanism, entire alpha>-1 family, and sharp constant quantify spectral stability not determined by qualitative spectrum/compactness statements. The natural invariant is the resolvent norm and epsilon-pseudospectral radial thickness, not an arbitrary chosen slice.
